The manipulation of time in the story is masterfully balanced and appropriate to its subject matter. Because the plot centers on a drawn-out, bureaucratic construction project spanning from early autumn to April, the author effectively uses **compression of time** to convey the exhausting, repetitive grind of the experience without boring the reader. Months of delays and adaptations are summarized in brief, punchy paragraphs (e.g., summarizing how different staff members adapted their routines, or how the "Membrane Theory" group chat slowly went quiet over the winter). 

This compression is balanced with moments where time slows down into real-time scenes or slightly **stretched** moments—such as the dinner conversation with Miriam's husband, the brief interaction with the air-quality consultant, and the final rainy afternoon where Miriam watches the ceiling to see if it will leak. This rhythm allows the reader to feel both the prolonged nature of the institutional incompetence and the quiet, immediate emotional toll it takes on the characters.
